property_summary: MinSum must never change after initialization; the mutant allows SetMinSum to reset it, violating the invariant that after any operation MinSum remains equal to its initial value.
After initialization, MinSum can never be increased; the mutant allows SetMinSum to be called repeatedly, enabling an increase.

After the contract is initialized via Initialized(), calling Collect should never alter MinSum; the mutant allows a subsequent call to SetMinSum to change MinSum, violating this post-initialization stability.
After initialization, MinSum cannot be decreased; the mutant allows SetMinSum to be called multiple times, enabling a decrease that changes the required minimum for a successful Collect.

After Collect succeeds, MinSum must stay equal to its value right after initialization; the mutant allows an early, post-initialization SetMinSum to change MinSum, so fuzzing a second SetMinSum+Collect makes Collect succeed in the reference but fail in the mutant (or vice‑versa) due to differing MinSum.
For any call to SetMinSum after initialization, the value of MinSum remains unchanged.

property_summary: For any sequence of calls through Collect, the value of c.MinSum() remains constant because the contract is initialized and MinSum cannot be changed after initialization; the bug allows a reentrant SetMinSum to alter MinSum during a Collect, violating this invariance.

After the contract is initialized, the value of MinSum never changes regardless of any sequence of external calls; the bug allows a reentrant SetMinSum call during Collect to modify MinSum, violating this invariant.
After initialization, MinSum must remain unchanged across any external call sequence; the bug allows reentrant SetMinSum inside Collect to alter MinSum, breaking that immutability.

After initialization, the value of MinSum can only change when some call to SetMinSum succeeds; the bug allows a reentrant chain through Collect to call SetMinSum without the nonReentrant lock, changing MinSum when a Collect would normally succeed.

After initialization, the value of MinSum is invariant across any call to Collect that does not revert; the buggy modifier allows reentrant SetMinSum during Collect, altering MinSum after a successful collect.
After SetMinSum(val), the stored MinSum equals the argument val in the correct contract; the buggy version stores val + 1, so MinSum != val for some input.
After initialization and SetMinSum, no further call can change MinSum; the buggy modifier allows a second SetMinSum to overwrite it.
After initialization, the value of MinSum must never change; the buggy modifier allows SetMinSum to be called again and overwrite it.

After initialization, if SetMinSum is called twice with different values, the stored MinSum must equal the value from the first call. The buggy modifier allows a second call to overwrite MinSum, violating this invariant.
After initialization, calling SetMinSum must revert for any input; the buggy modifier allows it to succeed and overwrite MinSum.

After initialization, calling SetMinSum twice with different values must leave MinSum equal to the first-set value; the buggy nonReentrant_ modifier allows the second call to succeed and overwrite it.

After initialisation, SetMinSum cannot be called again; the reference reentrancy guard correctly prevents nested re-entrant calls causing a revert, while the buggy version without the guard allows a re-entrant call to succeed and change MinSum.

After the contract is initialized, any call to SetMinSum must revert in the reference (because the initialisation flag forbids it), but a re-entrant call from a Put fallback can bypass the missing guard and change MinSum in the buggy version.

After initialization, the value of MinSum must remain unchanged after any call that attempts to call SetMinSum, but the buggy version without reentrancy check allows a re-entrant call via Put/fallback to change MinSum.

After initialization, calling SetMinSum directly must always revert; the buggy version without reentrancy check allows a re-entrant call from Put/fallback to change MinSum, violating the invariant that initialized MinSum is immutable.

After a successful external call to SetMinSum, the nonReentrant lock must be fully released (locked_ == false); the bug leaves locked_ stuck at true, permanently blocking any subsequent protected call.

After a successful call to SetMinSum, any subsequent call to a nonReentrant function (e.g., SetMinSum or Put) should succeed; the bug leaves locked_ stuck at true, so the next nonReentrant call reverts.

After a successful call to SetMinSum, a subsequent call to any nonReentrant function that depends on a successful external call must still succeed; the bug locks the contract after the first external call fails, so a following Put with an attached value reverts.

After any sequence of calls to SetMinSum, the total call count (successful plus reverted) equals the sum of calls made; the bug leaves the lock permanently set, causing all calls after the first to revert, thereby violating the invariant that a valid call to SetMinSum always succeeds regardless of prior history.
